slides.headline: THIS PASSWORD TIP ACTUALLY HELPS HACKERS
slides.kicker: THE TIP IS WRONG. HERE IS WHY.

caption:
A comma in your password went viral as a hacker defense, and 3.2 million people saw it before breakfast. 🔐

On Oct 4, an account called World of Engineering posted: 'always have a comma in your password, if your password leaks in a spreadsheet dump, the comma splits the row.' The tweet hit 3.2 million views, 45,000 likes, and 11,000 reposts in one morning. It does not work: when a hacker opens the leaked list in a spreadsheet, the comma breaks your password into two separate cells, both halves are still sitting right there in plain text. The comma does not hide a single character, it hands attackers your password pre-sliced.

Running a business? DM us 'AI' and we'll show you what real data protection actually looks like.

Sources: World of Engineering on X

pinned_comment: The real question: does a comma actually break a CSV? Yes, technically. Does it protect you from a real data breach? Not even close.

hook_sharpen.why: Only [2] states what the facts support—that 3.2M people were told this advice—instead of falsely claiming all 3.2M believed it when engagement metrics (45K likes from 3.2M viewers = 1.4%) prove far fewer actually fell for it. The comma absurdity still triggers 'wait, what?' in under 2 seconds without the lies.
